posts.body: I don't think there's a plugin for that, because the editor will only provide event commands for what is possible to do in the editor, which is 8 enemies.

The added enemies should be selectable as usual. If not, then that is probably a plugin conflict.
I did notice another bug though (sorry!). This part (line ~23042):
JavaScript:
for (const nme of M)
            nme.setLetter("");
...should include an
onBattleStart
call:
JavaScript:
for (const nme of M) {
            nme.setLetter("");
            nme.onBattleStart();
        }
This should make the reinforcements do something (e.g. attack) rather than just stand there. I think I had that in an earlier version but it got lost at some point.
If you're actually asking how to reference enemies 9+ through event commands: like others said, you need to use script calls for that. You may find the spreadsheet here helpful:
RPG Maker MV / MZ Script Call List
This Script Call list applies to both RPG Maker MV and RPG Maker MZ. Link here to see the entire list.    Supplementary Material for RPG Maker MZ: https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/rpg-maker-mz-script-call-reference.122501/  Have fun eventing~
forums.rpgmakerweb.com

posts.body:
Hm, OK. If you're using that many VisuStella plugins then you might be stuck with a VisuStella solution (or workaround).
I did a bit of searching and found this feature-rich Enemy Reinforcements plugin by taaspider:
TAA_EnemyReinforcements - v1.2.2
TAA_EnemyReinforcements - v1.2.2 Created by taaspider  Terms of Use Any plugins developed by taaspider are free for use for both commercial and noncommercial RPG Maker games, unless specified otherwise. Just remember to credit "taaspider".  Redistribution of parts or the whole of taaspider...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Looks worth a try!
I couldn't find an "add enemies mid-battle" feature in Visu Battle Core but a workaround might be:
Use Visu Battle Core's
<Extend: x>
tag to add enemies from 1+ other troop(s);
Right-click the enemies in those troops and choose "Appear Mid-Battle" to make them hidden.
Use the Enemy Appear command, or its Script equivalent, to make them show up mid-battle:
JavaScript:
// Make the 9th enemy appear, if it exists. (The first enemy is index 0.)
$gameTroop.members()[8]?.appear();
$gameTroop.makeUniqueNames();
That approach is more limited/awkward, but might be OK for your situation.
